function.mechanism: Provides sweetness and bulk as a polyol; its osmotic properties and low absorption also drive gastrointestinal tolerance limits at higher intakes.
common_food_categories: pressed mints and hard candy/cough drops
other foods under CFR use limits

adi.basis: No final EFSA ADI is published for the current re-evaluation dossiers EFSA-Q-2011-00646/00647 (output is null; re-evaluation ongoing).

efsa.key_finding: OpenEFSA records state mannitol is already authorised and under ongoing re-evaluation; scientific output is still in preparation.

fda.notes: For human food, mannitol is in Part 180 (interim food additive pending additional study) with category limits and a 20 g/day laxative warning statement; animal feed GRAS listing exists at 21 CFR 582.5470.

adi.basis: JECFA evaluation summary lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED.

concerns.summary: Dose-related osmotic laxative effects are recognized in both JECFA and CFR labeling conditions (high intake concern rather than systemic toxicity).

A 2025 prospective nested case-control analysis reported higher plasma mannitol/sorbitol associated with higher incident CHD risk, but this is an observational biomarker association and not direct proof of additive-intake causality.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA assigned ADI not specified (1986) and highlighted laxative tolerance as the key practical high-dose effect.
JECFA toxicological monograph reported no clear carcinogenicity-driving signal in reviewed long-term animal studies for food-use context.
A 2023 in-vitro human lymphocyte study found no significant genotoxic signal (chromosomal aberration or micronucleus increase) at tested concentrations.
No IARC monograph classification entry for mannitol was found in the current IARC list dataset.

populations: high consumers of sugar-free confectionery and chewing gum
children with high per-body-weight intake of polyol-containing products
individuals sensitive to osmotic laxative effects
adi_exceedance.notes: There is no numeric EFSA/JECFA ADI to compare against, but practical intolerance risk exists: JECFA reports a human laxative threshold around 10-20 g single dose and CFR requires warning labeling when foreseeable intake can reach 20 g/day.

risk_assessment.rationale: Current authoritative sources support continued authorization with the main concern being high-dose gastrointestinal tolerance (laxative effect). Lack of a completed EFSA re-evaluation and emerging observational cardiovascular biomarker associations justify caution, but available evidence does not support a moderate or high-risk classification.
key_factors: EFSA re-evaluation status is ongoing with no final output yet
21 CFR 180.25 allows use with explicit limits and mandatory high-intake laxative warning
JECFA ADI is not specified with long-standing evaluation history
No IARC classification entry identified for mannitol
Recent epidemiological association exists but is not causal proof of dietary additive harm
